head: a94e11bb008124df8227279a61162acfe77d0174
reasons: Phase c's only committed proof artifact is evidence/verifier.md, a hand-written narrative — not literal toolchain output. This project's own established convention for a build phase (change 0001, evidence/test.log, build.log, lint.log, each headed '# <command> — exit <code> — ...') is entirely absent here: no test.log, build.log or lint.log was committed for phase c of this change. verifier.md itself is a paraphrase (e.g. 'Last lines:' for the pytest run instead of full captured stdout) and explicitly states that two of the verifier's own verification commands were denied by the session's permission system, forcing it to re-run smaller ad hoc commands and write up the results from memory/observation rather than redirecting real command output to a file. A person cannot independently audit an exit code or a full test run here; they can only read the verifier's account of what it says it did.
classification_reasons: Spec tightness: tight — both of spec.md's flagged concerns (empty-input ValueError, Collection[float] parameter type) are closed with a decision, and Acceptance is fully measurable (mean([1,2,3,4])==2.5, mean([5])==5.0, mean([]) raises ValueError, mean({1.0,2.0,3.0})==2.0, 9 passed, ruff clean, silent compileall).

Blast radius: small — the diff touches exactly the files plan.md lists (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py) plus the change folder; no guardrail file, no sdlc.yaml risk_list item, no schema/contract/migration change; mean has no existing caller so add/divide/percent behaviour is unaffected.

Test coverage: mean is brand-new code with no pre-existing test covering it before this change — the build supplies its own four tests — so the third routine criterion (code the existing tests already cover) fails and the plan stays non-routine.
attempted: Intent: diff adds mean(values) returning the arithmetic mean as a float, decides the empty-input (ValueError) and parameter-type (Collection[float]) questions intent.md left open, exports it from __init__.py/__all__, and covers normal, single-element, empty and non-Sequence-Collection cases in tests/test_calc.py. This is exactly intent's Proposed outcome, nothing extra, nothing missing.

Spec and plan: read spec.md's Requirements, Design, Flagged concerns (both marked decided) and Acceptance, then plan.md's Files/Order of work/Proof. calc.py's mean body (guard clause raising ValueError, then divide(sum(values), len(values))) matches plan step 1 verbatim including the Collection import; __init__.py's import line and __all__ match step 2 exactly (alphabetical position between divide and percent); the four tests in tests/test_calc.py match step 3's names and assertions exactly, including the set-based test pinning Collection[float]. plan.md was amended in the same phase-c diff to reconcile the typing.Collection vs collections.abc.Collection wording with what the format-on-edit hook actually produced, so by HEAD the plan matches the diff.

Proof: compared the diff's four new tests against evidence/verifier.md (no test.log/build.log/lint.log exist for this phase, unlike change 0001's phase c/d). verifier.md names all four new tests individually (via 'pytest -k mean -v'), reports 9 passed matching the 8 dots for tests/test_calc.py plus 1 for tests/test_flag.py (consistent with the diff's test count), and exercises the changed behaviour (empty raises ValueError not ZeroDivisionError, set input works, add/divide/percent unaffected). However it is a narrative summary, not a captured raw log with the project's '# <command> — exit <code> — ...' header, and it self-reports that some of its own verification commands were blocked by the permission system and worked around — this is the verifier's claim about what it ran, not an independently auditable record. Escalated on this basis.

Blast radius: mean is additive and uncalled elsewhere; divide is called, not modified; __all__ gains one name in the correct alphabetical slot. No guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml), no sdlc.yaml risk_list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config), no schema or config file appears in the diff. status.yaml's diff is only the phase/timestamp bump expected at this point in the workflow.

Policies: coding-standards' export-pattern and type-hint rules are met (Collection[float] hint, alphabetical import/__all__ placement matching add/divide/percent); no new dependency, statistics.mean is not wrapped; security-baseline, ux-conventions and data-conventions are correctly inapplicable to a pure in-process arithmetic helper with no I/O, UI or stored data; definition-of-done's three commands are reported green in verifier.md (though see the Proof finding on how that's evidenced).

Tests: test_mean, test_mean_single_element, test_mean_empty and test_mean_accepts_non_sequence_collection each pin a distinct behaviour (correct averaging, single-element division, the explicit ValueError guard rather than a fallthrough ZeroDivisionError from divide, and the widened Collection[float]-not-Sequence contract via a set) — a bug in any of the guard condition, the divide call, or a Sequence-only implementation would fail one of them. No pre-existing test (test_add, test_divide_by_zero_raises, test_percent, test_percent_zero_whole_raises, tests/test_flag.py) is touched or weakened by this feature-type change.
